cases.prompt: I work in a plant and have an idea: our shift leads lose time collecting stop reasons on paper. I am not a digital specialist. Is this a real use case and how do I get it going?
cases.expected_output:
The first question asked is whether someone has already done this (catalogued use case).
The idea check is used in plain questions; unknown answers stay unknown, numbers without source stay unknown.
The outcome is one of: catalogued use case (Lane 1), recurring need handed to OD (Lane 2), or needs software or connection first (Lane 3).
No savings figure is invented.

cases.prompt: Intake accepted a demand from a plastics plant (fictional) for a downtime view on line 4. Please define the use case so it can go to requirements and the business case.
cases.expected_output:
The four phases Collect, Analyse, Assess, Control are followed with a control point each.
The use case carries plant, capability, process group, category and output asset.
The benefit is stated as a changed decision and classified, not as the dashboard itself.
A rejected alternative is named and a plant owner (role) is recorded.
The library is checked before anything is specified.

cases.prompt: Please run the full definition for an OEE calculation use case at our plant. Another plant already runs exactly that.
cases.expected_output:
A match to a library entry is recognised and the full definition is not run.
The request is routed to catalogue matching (Lane 1) or standardization.
The reason given is that a catalogued use case needs no definition.

cases.prompt: Plan the agenda, invite list and pre-read for next week's onboarding workshop at the plant.
cases.expected_output:
It is recognised that running the workshop is a workshop task.
The request is pointed to the workshop skill.
The questionnaire is offered only as content to run inside the workshop.
